summary: The root وري primarily means to conceal or hide something, especially fire or embers. It also refers to something being ignited or coming forth, like fire from wood.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: aor. يَرِى, inf. n. وَرْىٌ [and وُرِىٌّ and رِيَةٌ, K]; and وَرِىَ, aor. يَرِى; and; It (a زَنْد ) produced its fire. (Msb.) وَرِيَتْ بِكَ زِنَادِى, or وَرَتْ: see art. زند, and see وَقَدَ and زَهَرَ, and راى. قَدْحٌ لَا يُورِى: see خَيَّابٌ.

وَرَّى بِشَىْءٍ عَنْ شَىْءٍ [ He pretended, or made believe, a thing, instead of a thing which he meant: as is shown by the explanation of a trad. in the TA]. (S, art. عرض; save that the inf. n. is there mentioned instead of the pret.) وَرَّى عَنْ كَ َا, inf. n. تَوْرِيَةٌ, He alluded to such a thing equivocally, or ambiguously: equivocated respecting it: he meant such a thing and pretended another. (M, K.) التورية is also called الإِيهَامُ and التَّوْجِيهُ and التَّخْيِيلُ: (Kull, p.
He hid it, concealed it, or covered it. (S, Msb, K, &c.)
and and He made his زند to produce fire. (S, K.) See 1.
Purulent matter in the interior of the body: or [ an abscess; or] a severe ulcer that discharges purulent matter and blood. (M, K, TA.) وَرْيًا وَقُحَابًا: see قُحَابٌ.

وَرَائِى كَ َا Behind me is such a thing, as though it were a burden upon my back. مِنْ وَرَآءَ وَرَآءَ From behind a thing covering, or concealing. (TA.) فُلَانٌ مِنْ وَرَآءِ فُلَانٍ Such a one is an aider of such a one: or a follower. (Ham, p. 206.) اَللّٰهُ مِنْ وَرَائِكَ God is seeking after thee, and watching, or lying in wait, for thee. (Ham, p. 206.) See also an ex. in the first paragraph of art. فتل.
The Book of the Law revealed to Moses. (Bd, iii. 2; &c.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
